items.summary: Path traversal and NULL-byte flaws in Fortinet FortiMail let an unauthenticated remote attacker write arbitrary files to the appliance via crafted HTTP/HTTPS requests. Fortinet confirmed active zero-day exploitation; added to the CISA KEV catalog on October 1 — patch immediately.

Authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (vManage) via improper URI-encoding handling lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the management API with administrator privileges — no workaround exists. Cisco confirmed active exploitation in September; CISA added it to KEV on September 30 with an October 3 federal remediation deadline.

Missing authentication in the Mooncake HTTP metadata server's /metadata handler (through 0.3.13.post1) allows unauthenticated attackers to read, overwrite and delete data-transfer state on the distributed cache layer. Disclosed October 2.

Heap-based buffer overflow in F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager gives unauthenticated remote code execution when APM is configured as an OAuth Authorization Server (17.1.0–17.1.3, 17.5.0–17.5.1, 21.1.0). Actively exploited zero-day; on the CISA KEV catalog since September 22 — restricting the management interface does not mitigate it.

Pre-authentication directory traversal and file upload in the Check Point Security Management web service allows arbitrary-path script execution and arbitrary Java class load on Management, Log and SmartEvent servers. Check Point confirmed active exploitation in the wild; added to the CISA KEV catalog on September 22.
